subject: Capacity ramp & OEM lead-time visibility for BRIO-4521
messages:
From: Lara Gomez <lara.gomez@brio.ai>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Brio procurement <procurement@brio.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity ramp & OEM lead-time visibility for BRIO-4521

Hi Vivek,

Hope you're well — excited to be moving forward on BRIO-4521. Our procurement and infra teams are aligning schedules and we need tighter ETA visibility so we can lock our internal launch cadence. Two asks to start: 

1) Can you confirm the targeted start window for the Dedicated pool footprint that was scoped in the term sheet (we're expecting capacity to be available between mid-August and end‑September)?
2) We need the latest OEM lead-time and slot commitments (AtlasCompute) and what cloud backstop options Redwood can put in place if hardware slips — specifically whether a short-term cloud burst with a 30-day cancel is feasible and costed.

I've attached our Q3 demand forecast (BRIO_Demand_Forecast_Q3.xlsx) so you can see ramp profile (week-by-week token estimates). If helpful, let's schedule a 30-min call this week to walk the numbers and any pre-pay sizing assumptions.

Thanks — Lara
Lara Gomez
Head of Platform 
BrioAI

Attachment: BRIO_Demand_Forecast_Q3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Lara Gomez <lara.gomez@brio.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity ramp & OEM lead-time visibility for BRIO-4521

Lara — thanks for the forecast and the clear asks. High level: we can meet a mid-August soft-start for a limited Dedicated slab and target full ramp by late-September, but that depends on AtlasCompute slot confirmation and customs/ship windows for dedicated on-prem hardware.

Immediate next steps I propose:
- Internal sizing call to confirm the peak concurrent sequences and sustained tokens/day you used in the forecast (30-min).
- We'll concurrently request a firm slot ETA from AtlasCompute and a provisional cloud-burst quote from our Cloud Partnerships team (GCP / AWS) that supports a ~30-day cancellable reservation for the same window.
- Redwood will prepare a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that ties milestones to purchase/commit triggers; I'll loop Karthik to own the MAP delivery.

Can you do Thursday 5/31 at 10:00 PT? If not, propose two alternatives. Attaching a draft MAP template for transparency.

— Vivek
VP, Strategic Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Draft_MAP_BRIO-4521.docx (docx, 3 pages)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Atlas & cloud backstop action items (BRIO-4521)

Team — quick internal note after looping through the forecast:

1) AtlasCompute lead-time request: Will Park (sales@atlascompute.com) — ask for two items: (a) firm slot date (ETA by ship + customs) for the SKU set Brio requested, (b) ability to hold a soft-reserve for 60 days with partial deposit (we should push for 30-day cancel, but prepare deposit fallback).

2) Cloud backstop: reach out to GCP account team for a 30-day cancellable committed instance / capacity block sized to the 80th percentile week in the forecast. Request pricing in both hourly burst and 30-day prepay buckets.

3) Sizing parameters we need from Brio on the call: peak concurrent token streams, average seq length, p95 latency SLO target, and any planned eval/inference batching (that changes slot requirements).

Deliverables & owners:
- Karthik: AtlasCompute slot confirmation + draft RFP to vendor (due 2028-06-05)
- Laura: Cloud backstop pricing options and preliminary cost delta matrix (due 2028-06-04)
- Vivek: Draft MAP to send to Brio after call (due 2028-06-05)

I'll open a tracker in the procurement board and include links to quotes when available.

— Karthik
Head of Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference

From: Lara Gomez <lara.gomez@brio.ai>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Brio procurement <procurement@brio.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Jun 2028 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity ramp & OEM lead-time visibility for BRIO-4521

Thanks Vivek — Thursday doesn't work for us, but Friday 6/4 09:00 PT is good.

Couple quick clarifications ahead of the call:
- The forecast uses an average sequence length of 280 tokens with peak concurrent streams of ~420 and a p95 latency target of 250ms.
- Brio prefers not to pre-pay large deposits; our procurement will consider a modest deposit if it materially shortens lead time risk.

Please share the MAP and any initial vendor questions in advance; that will speed the call.

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Lara Gomez <lara.gomez@brio.ai>, Will Park <will.park@atlascompute.com>
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 08 Jun 2028 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Atlas quote & short-term backstop options (BRIO-4521)

Lara / Will — following our call last Friday, attaching AtlasCompute_quote_v3.pdf which includes two lead-time lanes (standard ship: ETA 8/20–9/05; expedited slot with partial deposit: ETA 8/01–8/10).

Laura here — quick summary of options we discussed:
- Option A (Preferred): Secure Atlas expedited slot with 20% deposit — guarantees hardware arrival early August.
- Option B (Lower risk): Standard Atlas slot + GCP cancellable burst for first 30 days post-start (we've asked GCP for pricing; preliminary delta in the shared drive link).

We've opened the procurement ticket and will circulate the MAP for signatures once Brio confirms which lane they prefer. If Brio wants to avoid deposit, Option B keeps launch protected but adds cloud cost for the first 4–6 weeks.

Attachment: AtlasCompute_quote_v3.pdf (pdf, 6 pages)

— Laura Bennett
Director, Partnerships
Redwood Inference
